1	# AI Model Capability Benchmark Data
     2	
     3	## Overview
     4	Normalized benchmark scores for 10 large language models across 8 capability dimensions, designed for parallel coordinates visualization. Models span 5 families (GPT, Claude, Gemini, LLaMA, Qwen) with both flagship and lightweight variants per family.
     5	
     6	## Data Source
     7	
     8	### model_benchmarks
     9	Each record represents one AI model with the following fields:
    10	- **model** (string): Model name, e.g., "GPT-4o", "Claude 3.5 Sonnet"
    11	- **family** (string): Model family grouping — one of GPT, Claude, Gemini, LLaMA, Qwen
    12	- **Reasoning** (integer, 0-100): Complex multi-step reasoning benchmark score
    13	- **Code Generation** (integer, 0-100): Programming and code synthesis score
    14	- **Math / Quantitative** (integer, 0-100): Mathematical problem-solving score
    15	- **Language Understanding** (integer, 0-100): NLU and reading comprehension score
    16	- **Multimodal Understanding** (integer, 0-100): Image, video, and cross-modal reasoning score
    17	- **Instruction Following** (integer, 0-100): Adherence to complex user instructions
    18	- **Inference Speed** (integer, 0-100): Normalized throughput (higher = faster)
    19	- **Knowledge Recall** (integer, 0-100): Factual knowledge and world knowledge retrieval
    20	
    21	All scores are normalized to a 0-100 scale for cross-dimension comparability.
    22	
    23	## Data Notes
    24	- Scores are synthetic composites inspired by publicly reported benchmarks (MMLU, HumanEval, GSM8K, MMMU, MT-Bench, etc.) but do not correspond to exact published numbers.
    25	- Inference Speed is inversely related to model size; lightweight variants score higher.
    26	- Multimodal scores for text-only-focused models (LLaMA, Qwen) are notably lower, reflecting limited native multimodal capability.
    27	- Each family includes one flagship and one smaller/faster variant to illustrate capability-efficiency trade-offs.

Supports JavaScript API integration, CLI rendering to SVG/PNG/PDF, theming, configuration, and accessibility features. Essential for documentation, technical diagrams, project planning, system architecture, and visual communication. 4 --- 5 6 # Mermaid.js v11 7 8 ## Overview 9 10 Create text-based diagrams using Mermaid.js v11 declarative syntax. Convert code to SVG/PNG/PDF via CLI or render in browsers/markdown files. 11 12 ## Quick Start 13 14 **Basic Diagram Structure:** 15 ``` 16 {diagram-type} 17 {diagram-content} 18 ``` 19 20 **Common Diagram Types:** 21 - `flowchart` - Process flows, decision trees 22 - `sequenceDiagram` - Actor interactions, API flows 23 - `classDiagram` - OOP structures, data models 24 - `stateDiagram` - State machines, workflows 25 - `erDiagram` - Database relationships 26 - `gantt` - Project timelines 27 - `journey` - User experience flows 28 29 See `references/diagram-types.md` for all 24+ types with syntax. 30 31 ## Creating Diagrams 32 33 **Inline Markdown Code Blocks:** 34 ````markdown 35 ```mermaid 36 flowchart TD 37 A[Start] --> B{Decision} 38 B -->|Yes| C[Action] 39 B -->|No| D[End] 40 ``` 41 ```` 42 43 **Configuration via Frontmatter:** 44 ````markdown 45 ```mermaid 46 --- 47 theme: dark 48 --- 49 flowchart LR 50 A --> B 51 ``` 52 ```` 53 54 **Comments:** Use `%% ` prefix for single-line comments. 55 56 ## CLI Usage 57 58 Convert `.mmd` files to images: 59 ```bash 60 # Installation 61 npm install -g @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli 62 63 # Basic conversion 64 mmdc -i diagram.mmd -o diagram.svg 65 66 # With theme and background 67 mmdc -i input.mmd -o output.png -t dark -b transparent 68 69 # Custom styling 70 mmdc -i diagram.mmd --cssFile style.css -o output.svg 71 ``` 72 73 See `references/cli-usage.md` for Docker, batch processing, and advanced workflows. 74 75 ## JavaScript Integration 76 77 **HTML Embedding:** 78 ```html 79

1	# Mermaid.js Diagram Types
     2	
     3	Comprehensive syntax reference for all 24+ diagram types in Mermaid.js v11.
     4	
     5	## Core Diagrams
     6	
     7	### Flowchart
     8	Process flows, decision trees, workflows.
     9	
    10	**Syntax:**
    11	```
    12	flowchart {direction}
    13	  {nodeId}[{label}] {arrow} {nodeId}[{label}]
    14	```
    15	
    16	**Directions:** TB/TD (top-bottom), BT, LR (left-right), RL
    17	**Shapes:** `()` round, `[]` rect, `{}` diamond, `{{}}` hexagon, `(())` circle
    18	**Arrows:** `-->` solid, `-.->` dotted, `==>` thick
    19	**Subgraphs:** Group related nodes
    20	
    21	### Sequence Diagram
    22	Actor interactions, API flows, message sequences.
    23	
    24	**Syntax:**
    25	```
    26	sequenceDiagram
    27	  participant A as Actor
    28	  A->>B: Message
    29	  activate B
    30	  B-->>A: Response
    31	  deactivate B
    32	```
    33	
    34	**Arrows:** `->` solid, `->>` arrow, `-->` dotted, `-x` cross, `-)` async
    35	**Features:** Loops, alternatives, parallel, optional, critical regions
    36	
    37	### Class Diagram
    38	OOP structures, inheritance, relationships.
    39	
    40	**Syntax:**
    41	```
    42	classDiagram
    43	  class Animal {
    44	    +String name
    45	    -int age
    46	    +void eat()
    47	  }
    48	  Animal <|-- Dog : inherits
    49	```
    50	
    51	**Visibility:** `+` public, `-` private, `#` protected, `~` package
    52	**Relationships:** `<|--` inheritance, `*--` composition, `o--` aggregation, `-->` association
    53	
    54	### State Diagram
    55	State machines, transitions, workflows.
    56	
    57	**Syntax:**
    58	```
    59	stateDiagram-v2
    60	  [*] --> State1
    61	  State1 --> State2 : transition
    62	  State2 --> [*]
    63	```
    64	
    65	**Features:** Composite states, choice points, forks/joins, concurrency
    66	
    67	### ER Diagram
    68	Database relationships, schemas.
    69	
    70	**Syntax:**
    71	```
    72	erDiagram
    73	  CUSTOMER ||--o{ ORDER : places
    74	  ORDER ||--|{ LINE_ITEM : contains
    75	```
    76	
    77	**Cardinality:** `||` one, `|o` zero-one, `}|` one-many, `}o` zero-many
    78	
    79	## Planning Diagrams
    80	
    81	### Gantt Chart
    82	Project timelines, schedules.
    83	
    84	**Syntax:**
    85	```
    86	gantt
    87	  title Project
    88	  dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD
    89	  section Phase1
    90	    Task1 :done, 2024-01-01, 5d
    91	    Task2 :active, after Task1, 3d
    92	```
    93	
    94	**Status:** `done`, `active`, `crit`, `milestone`
    95	
    96	### User Journey
    97	Experience flows, satisfaction tracking.
    98	
    99	**Syntax:**
   100	```
   101	journey
   102	  title User Journey
   103	  section Shopping
   104	    Browse: 5: Customer
   105	    Add to cart: 3: Customer, System
   106	```
   107	
   108	**Scores:** 1-5 satisfaction levels
   109	
   110	### Kanban
   111	Task boards, workflow stages.
   112	
   113	**Syntax:**
   114	```
   115	kanban
   116	  Todo[Task Board]
   117	    task1[Implement API]
   118	    @{ assigned: "Dev1", priority: "High" }
   119	  InProgress[In Progress]
   120	    task2[Fix bug]
   121	```
   122	
   123	### Quadrant Chart
   124	Prioritization, trend analysis.
   125	
   126	**Syntax:**
   127	```
   128	quadrantChart
   129	  x-axis Low --> High
   130	  y-axis Low --> High
   131	  Item A: [0.3, 0.6]
   132	```
   133	
   134	## Architecture Diagrams
   135	
   136	### C4 Diagram
   137	System architecture, components.
   138	
   139	**Syntax:**
   140	```
   141	C4Context
   142	  Person(user, "User")
   143	  System(app, "Application")
   144	  Rel(user, app, "Uses")
   145	```
   146	
   147	### Architecture Diagram
   148	Cloud infrastructure, services.
   149	
   150	**Syntax:**
   151	```
   152	architecture-beta
   153	  service api(server)[API]
   154	  service db(database)[Database]
   155	  api:R --> L:db
   156	```
   157	
   158	**Icons:** cloud, database, disk, internet, server, or iconify.design icons
   159	
   160	### Block Diagram
   161	Module dependencies, networks.
   162	
   163	**Syntax:**
   164	```
   165	block-beta
   166	  columns 3
   167	  a["Block A"] b["Block B"]
   168	  a --> b
   169	```
   170	
   171	**Shapes:** rounded, stadium, cylinder, diamond, trapezoid, hexagon
   172	
   173	## Data Visualization
   174	
   175	### Pie Chart
   176	Proportions, distributions.
   177	
   178	**Syntax:**
   179	```
   180	pie showData
   181	  "Category A" : 45.5
   182	  "Category B" : 30.0
   183	```
   184	
   185	### XY Chart
   186	Trends, comparisons.
   187	
   188	**Syntax:**
   189	```
   190	xychart-beta
   191	  x-axis [jan, feb, mar]
   192	  y-axis "Sales" 0 --> 100
   193	  line [30, 45, 60]
   194	  bar [25, 40, 55]
   195	```
   196	
   197	### Sankey
   198	Flow visualization, resource allocation.
   199	
   200	**Syntax:**
   201	```
   202	sankey-beta
   203	  Source,Target,Value
   204	  A,B,10
   205	  B,C,5
   206	```
   207	
   208	### Radar Chart
   209	Multi-dimensional comparison.
   210	
   211	**Syntax:**
   212	```
   213	radar-beta
   214	  axis Skill1, Skill2, Skill3
   215	  curve Team1{3,4,5}
   216	  curve Team2{4,3,4}
   217	```
   218	
   219	### Treemap
   220	Hierarchical proportions.
   221	
   222	**Syntax:**
   223	```
   224	treemap-beta
   225	  "Root"
   226	    "Category A"
   227	      "Item 1": 100
   228	      "Item 2": 200
   229	```
   230	
   231	## Technical Diagrams
   232	
   233	### Git Graph
   234	Branching strategies, workflows.
   235	
   236	**Syntax:**
   237	```
   238	gitGraph
   239	  commit
   240	  branch develop
   241	  checkout develop
   242	  commit
   243	  checkout main
   244	  merge develop
   245	```
   246	
   247	### Timeline
   248	Chronological events, milestones.
   249	
   250	**Syntax:**
   251	```
   252	timeline
   253	  2024 : Event A : Event B
   254	  2025 : Event C
   255	```
   256	
   257	### Packet Diagram
   258	Network protocols, structures.
   259	
   260	**Syntax:**
   261	```
   262	packet-beta
   263	  0-15: "Header"
   264	  16-31: "Data"
   265	```
   266	
   267	### ZenUML Sequence
   268	Alternative sequence syntax.
   269	
   270	**Syntax:**
   271	```
   272	zenuml
   273	  A.method() {
   274	    B.process()
   275	    return result
   276	  }
   277	```
   278	
   279	### Mindmap
   280	Brainstorming, hierarchies.
   281	
   282	**Syntax:**
   283	```
   284	mindmap
   285	  root((Central Idea))
   286	    Branch 1
   287	      Sub 1
   288	      Sub 2
   289	    Branch 2
   290	```
   291	
   292	### Requirement Diagram
   293	SysML requirements, traceability.
   294	
   295	**Syntax:**
   296	```
   297	requirementDiagram
   298	  requirement req1 {
   299	    id: R1
   300	    text: User shall login
   301	    risk: Medium
   302	  }
   303	```
   304	
   305	## Quick Reference
   306	
   307	| Type | Best For | Complexity |
   308	|------|----------|------------|
   309	| Flowchart | Processes | Low |
   310	| Sequence | Interactions | Medium |
   311	| Class | OOP | High |
   312	| State | Behaviors | Medium |
   313	| ER | Databases | Low |
   314	| Gantt | Timelines | Medium |
   315	| Architecture | Systems | High |

import json
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
import numpy as np

# Load data
with open('/app/benchmark/source_data.json') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

models = data['model_benchmarks']['data']
dims = data['model_benchmarks']['dimensions']

# Color mapping by family
family_colors = {
    'GPT': '#1f77b4',      # blue
    'Claude': '#9467bd',   # purple
    'Gemini': '#2ca02c',   # green
    'LLaMA': '#ff7f0e',    # orange
    'Qwen': '#d62728',     # red
}

# Determine top models by average score across all dimensions
def avg_score(m):
    return sum(m[d] for d in dims) / len(dims)

avg_scores = {m['model']: avg_score(m) for m in models}
top_models = set(sorted(avg_scores, key=avg_scores.get, reverse=True)[:3])

# Axes positions
x_positions = np.arange(len(dims))

# Setup figure with publication-ready styling
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(13, 8), dpi=150)
fig.patch.set_facecolor('white')
ax.set_facecolor('white')

# Draw grid lines for y-axis
for y in range(0, 101, 20):
    ax.axhline(y=y, color='#e8e8e8', linewidth=0.6, zorder=0)

# Draw vertical axes lines
for x in x_positions:
    ax.axvline(x=x, color='#cccccc', linewidth=0.8, zorder=1)
    # Axis tick labels at top and bottom
    ax.text(x, -5, str(0), ha='center', va='top', fontsize=8, color='#666666')
    ax.text(x, 105, str(100), ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=8, color='#666666')

# Draw model polylines
for m in models:
    y_vals = [m[d] for d in dims]
    color = family_colors[m['family']]
    is_top = m['model'] in top_models
    lw = 3.0 if is_top else 1.2
    alpha = 1.0 if is_top else 0.6
    zorder = 10 if is_top else 5
    
    ax.plot(x_positions, y_vals, color=color, linewidth=lw, alpha=alpha, zorder=zorder, solid_capstyle='round')
    
    # Add markers
    ms = 6 if is_top else 3
    ax.scatter(x_positions, y_vals, color=color, s=ms**2, alpha=alpha, zorder=zorder+1, edgecolors='white', linewidths=0.5)

# Axis labels
ax.set_xticks(x_positions)
ax.set_xticklabels(dims, fontsize=10, fontweight='semibold', color='#222222')
ax.set_xlim(-0.5, len(dims)-0.5)
ax.set_ylim(0, 100)
ax.set_yticks(range(0, 101, 20))
ax.set_yticklabels([str(y) for y in range(0, 101, 20)], fontsize=9, color='#444444')
ax.set_ylabel('Normalized Score (0–100)', fontsize=12, fontweight='semibold', color='#222222')

# Remove top and right spines
for spine in ['top', 'right']:
    ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['left'].set_color('#bbbbbb')
ax.spines['bottom'].set_color('#bbbbbb')

# Title
ax.set_title('AI Model Capability Benchmarks Across 8 Dimensions', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', color='#1a1a1a', pad=20)

# Legend by family
legend_patches = [
    mpatches.Patch(color=family_colors[f], label=f) for f in family_colors
]
legend = ax.legend(
    handles=legend_patches,
    title='Model Family',
    loc='upper center',
    bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.12),
    ncol=5,
    frameon=True,
    fancybox=False,
    edgecolor='#cccccc',
    fontsize=10,
    title_fontsize=11
)

# Annotation box
ax.text(
    0.02, 0.98,
    'Thicker lines highlight top-performing models\n(highest average scores across all dimensions)',
    transform=ax.transAxes,
    fontsize=9,
    color='#555555',
    verticalalignment='top',
    bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.4', facecolor='#f8f8f8', edgecolor='#cccccc', linewidth=0.8)
)

# Tight layout to fit legend below
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.08, 1, 1])

# Save
fig.savefig('/app/output/result.png', dpi=200, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='white', edgecolor='none')
plt.close(fig)
print('Saved to /app/output/result.png')
